question: Can a team of agents improve a blind transit search faster than hand tuning, and does the improved search recover planets the TESS team announced after 2026-07-01?

record.title: Quick dev run of pipelines/baseline.py
Full dev run of pipelines/baseline.py
Promote pipelines/baseline.py to champion
Can agents raise blind transit-search recall at a fixed 5% false-alarm rate faster than hand tuning, and does the gain hold on planets announced after 2026-07-01?
record.body: Measured outcome: dev score (mean of known-planet and injected-transit recall at 5% control false alarms), then one blind holdout score. Baseline champion dev-8f6a421c scores 0.2224 (planet recall 0.152, injection recall 0.293) at 11.7 s per star.

record.title: A time-windowed sliding Tukey biweight filter is the best general-purpose detrender for transit discovery
record.body: Hippke et al. benchmarked all common detrending methods on hundreds of hard, small-radius-ratio Kepler/K2/TESS planets and found that a time-windowed biweight slider recovered 99% (Kepler) and 94% (K2) of the shallowest planets. For us: use a wotan biweight with a time window (not a fixed number of points), and tune the window against transit duration on dev.

record.title: TLS gives higher detection efficiency than BLS for small planets
record.body: TLS models limb-darkened ingress/egress on the unbinned phase fold and is tuned for SDE on small planets. It runs about as fast as BLS on K2 light curves when trial durations are restricted, and the paper derives an SDE threshold from Earth-size injection-recovery. For us: switching from BLS to TLS, with a restricted duration grid, could raise recall of shallow injections.

record.title: TLS recovers shallow transits that BLS misses on the same light curve
record.body: On the K2SFF light curve of K2-32, an extra 1 Earth-radius signal reached SDE_TLS=13.2 but only SDE_BLS=8.9, below common thresholds. Better detrending (EVEREST) raised SDE_TLS to 26.1. For us: both the search statistic and the detrending quality decide whether near-threshold signals are found.

record.title: A transit-model matched search beats BLS and TLS at low SNR
record.body: CETRA first searches linear time with a physical transit model and then phase-folds. On synthetic light curves it found at least 20% more low-SNR transits than TLS, especially at long periods, and it is much faster at high cadence. For us: a matched-filter, single-event-statistic search followed by period folding is worth trying beyond TLS.

record.title: Single-sector TESS FFI transit searches with a dedicated detrend-plus-search pipeline recover small planets
record.body: NEMESIS detrended single-sector FFI photometry of 33k nearby M dwarfs (sectors 1-5, 30-min cadence) and searched it, giving 183 threshold crossings and 29 candidates (1.26-5.31 Earth radii, P=1.25-6.84 d). For us: this is a reference design for exactly our setting of one sector of FFI data.

record.title: Correlated (red) noise lowers transit-survey detection yields, and detectability scales with the number of transits
record.body: Smith et al. modelled SuperWASP yields under realistic red noise and found that the best way to limit its effect is to raise SNR by observing more transits per candidate. For us: within one sector, scoring with a red-noise-aware SNR (per-transit noise measured on transit timescales, not white rms/sqrt(N)) should cut false alarms from systematics.

record.title: Time-averaging (rms vs bin size) is a sound correlated-noise estimator; residual permutation is not
record.body: Cubillos et al. used injection-retrieval to show that time-averaging and wavelet-likelihood significantly improve uncertainty estimates under correlated noise, while residual permutation is unsound. For us: use a time-averaged (binned-rms beta-factor) noise estimate at the transit-duration scale when normalising the detection score.

record.title: Automated flux-level vetting can reject noise and systematic false alarms in TESS searches while keeping high completeness
record.body: LEO-Vetter, which follows the Kepler Robovetter, reached 91% completeness and 97% reliability against noise/systematic false alarms on simulated TESS signals. For us: cheap flux-level checks (odd/even, transit-shape, individual-event consistency) applied to the score could lower the control-star false-alarm threshold.

record.title: [agent-generated] Global-SDE scoring, not detection, loses deep planets; single-event systematics set the control threshold
record.body: Evidence (run dev-8f6a421c; scripts in lab/analysis/): planets >10000 ppm recovered only 15/66. I re-ran baseline.search on the 8 deepest misses (TIC 309845124, 111778581, 115018003, 437346961, 31061885, 347866089, 12999193, 60091800). In all 8 the rank-1 signal MATCHES the TOI period and epoch, but SDE = 7.2-16.5, below threshold 17.07. SDE = (max-mean)/std of the BLS power spectrum, so a strong signal's aliases inflate the std and the score stops rising with depth. On the control side (80-star random dev_controls sample, lab/analysis/q1_controls_vs_injections_n80.json) the highest-SDE controls are long-period (7-14 d) peaks with only 1-2 in-transit events (SDE 38.7, 18.1, 18.0; ntransits 1,1,1): single dips, gap edges or ramps. In the same sample, 55% of injections match but only 41% clear the 95% control quantile. A robust (median/MAD) SDE on the BLS snr objective already raises this to 44% without other changes; a naive depth/MAD SNR does worse (20%) because the systematic single events are deep. So the score needs both a depth-SNR term and a single-event penalty.

data.mechanism: Replace global SDE with a per-signal score: robust depth SNR (depth / MAD * sqrt(n_in_transit)) times a consistency factor that penalises signals with fewer than 3 transits with data, or where one event carries most of the power (max single-event SNR / total SNR). Compute it separately for each iterative signal, not reusing the spectrum-wide SDE. This lets deep, already-detected planets clear the threshold and pushes 1-2-event systematics below it.
data.expected_score_gain: +0.10 (range +0.06 to +0.15); mainly planet recall 0.15 -> ~0.30, with injection recall up to the ~0.55 detection ceiling
data.test: Quick: offline rescoring of the saved 80+80 sample plus the 8 deep misses (~3 min), then planetlab experiment --quick (~3-7 min). Go/no-go: score > 0.1575 quick baseline and the 8 deep misses recovered. Full: full dev run (~18 min) for promotion on matched targets.

record.title: [agent-generated] Weak detrending and no systematics masking let short-period variability and gap-edge events take the BLS peak
record.body: Evidence (80-star random dev_controls sample, lab/analysis/q1_controls_vs_injections_n80.json): 45% of injected transits are never matched by the rank-1 BLS peak. That is a detection-ceiling loss that no rescoring can fix. The unmatched peaks fall into two groups. (a) Short-period peaks at P = 0.54-0.72 d with the maximum 3.8 h duration and 25-68 'transits'. These are stellar variability or rotation left over after the 1-day running median (knots every 30 cadences), which is too stiff for sub-day variability. (b) Long-period peaks at P = 11-14 d with 1-4 events: gap edges, momentum dumps or scattered-light ramps. Several lost injections had high expected SNR (depth/MAD*sqrt(n_in) of about 110, 33, 14, 10.8) but were displaced by these systematics. Several targets also span about 51 d with 3-4 gaps, so gap-edge handling matters. Injected durations go up to about 4.9 h, but the duration grid tops out at 3.8 h (0.16 d) and has only 3 steps.

data.mechanism: Use a more flexible, outlier-robust detrend (Tukey biweight or robust spline, window about 0.5 d, i.e. about 3x the longest transit) with iterative upward/downward sigma-clipping. Mask about 0.3 d at every gap edge and at sector start/end. Widen and densify the duration grid (0.03-0.22 d, about 6 steps). Together these remove the variability and gap-edge peaks that currently beat real transits in the BLS spectrum.
data.expected_score_gain: +0.06 (range +0.03 to +0.10); mainly injection recall, by raising the match ceiling from about 0.55 toward 0.70; planet recall rises less unless combined with the scoring fix
data.test: Quick: on the saved 80-star sample, measure the rank-1 match rate for injections (baseline 0.55) and the 95% control quantile with the new detrend (~3 min offline), then planetlab experiment --quick (~3-7 min; runtime must stay near 12 s/star, since the denser duration grid costs CPU). Full: full dev run (~18 min). Also test it combined with the competing scoring hypothesis, because the two gains should be roughly additive.

record.title: [agent-generated] H1+H2 combined: per-signal SNR scoring with event-count penalty on top of biweight detrend, gap-edge masking and wider duration grid
record.body: PI-composed from analyst H1 and H2. They target disjoint failure modes (under-scored detected planets vs never-detected injections), so the gains may add. Testing the combination checks additivity and interaction (e.g. better detrending lowers the robust noise used by H1's SNR).

record.title: Round 1 plan: test H1, H2 and H3 (H1+H2) in parallel
record.body: Options considered: H1 per-signal SNR scoring with single-event penalty (+0.10 expected, ~25 min); H2 biweight detrend + gap-edge masking + wider duration grid (+0.06, ~30 min); H3 = H1+H2 combined (+0.14 if additive, ~30 min); TLS instead of BLS (E2,E3; injection-recall gain, runtime risk); red-noise binned-scatter SNR (E6,E7; overlaps H1); vetting checks folded into score (E8); CETRA matched search (E4; large rewrite). Chosen: H1, H2, H3. Why: the analyst's diagnosis is direct evidence on our own data, these address the two measured dominant losses (8/8 deep misses are scoring failures; 45% of injections lose to artifact peaks), they are cheap (~25-30 min each), and running the combination alongside the parts measures additivity in one round. TLS is deferred because it costs runtime and its gain depends on detrending (E3) — better tested on top of the round-1 winner. Red-noise SNR and E8 vetting are deferred as refinements of H1's scoring. CETRA deferred as a big rewrite. Each engineer: quick run first, full run only if quick beats 0.1575.

record.body: Recorded manually: planetlab experiment crashed after saving the run (harness.evaluate returns the run without 'outcomes', so lab.compare_to_champion raises KeyError). vs_champion computed with lab.paired_comparison against quick baseline dev-8f85629b from the saved run files.

record.title: Round 1: H1 passes its quick test (0.414 vs 0.1575) but cannot be promoted; H2/H3 untested; lab blocked by policy
record.body: What changed: nothing promoted. Champion is still baseline dev-8f6a421c (0.2224). Learned: H1 (per-signal robust SNR plus event-count penalty) scored 0.414 on the quick test (dev-55fcddcf) against 0.1575 for the baseline quick run; paired comparison gained 52, lost 2. This supports the analyst's claim that the scoring step, not detection, is the dominant loss. Of the 8 deep misses, 4 were in the quick subset and 3 of those were recovered. TIC 111778581 (P=11.4 d) is still missed. The likely cause, not yet confirmed, is that the fewer-than-3-transits penalty suppresses real long-period planets. Treat this as a known risk of H1. Blockers (all need a person): (1) the full dev run of H1 was refused with 'Full-experiment budget of 2 is spent', although runs/ holds only one full run (the baseline). The budget accounting looks wrong or is shared across sessions. (2) The file-write policy refused the H2 and H3 engineers' writes to pipelines/ with contradictory messages, so both are untested. (3) A harness bug: planetlab experiment raises KeyError in compare_to_champion after saving the run, because evaluate() returns the run without outcomes. R3 was therefore recorded by hand from the run files and needs the skeptic to check it. Reopened assumption: P1 assumed that H1's single-event penalty only removes systematics. TIC 111778581 suggests it also costs real long-period planets. Next round should: once the blockers are fixed, run H1 full, send it to the skeptic, then test H3 and an H1 variant whose penalty uses per-event consistency instead of a hard count of 3 transits.

record.title: Skeptic review of H1 promotion (dev-7227ffda): CAUTION, safe to promote with caveats
record.body: Verdict CAUTION, with no blocking risks. (1) Metrics check: runs/dev-7227ffda.json and dev-55fcddcf.json have pipeline sha 7bd79dd1, which matches the current pipelines/h1_robust_snr.py. Recounting the outcomes gives planet 90/231=0.3896, injected 123/399=0.3083, score 0.3489. Rerunning lab.paired_comparison against dev-8f6a421c gives gained 94, lost 33, p=5.7e-8 (the record shows 0.0 only because of rounding). R3 also reproduces (52/2 vs dev-8f85629b). The control FA count of 20/399 cannot be checked independently because control outcomes are not saved. (2) Leakage: the diff against baseline only replaces the score with robust depth SNR x count factor x dominance factor. It has no TICs, periods, file I/O or split access, and the threshold is set by the harness from controls. Mild design-on-dev risk: MIN_EVENTS=3 and the 1/sqrt(3) dominance factor were chosen after inspecting dev controls and deep misses, so the blind evaluation is the real test. The quick split overstated the gain: +0.2565 quick vs +0.1265 full. Runtime 11.67 -> 13.73 s/star (1.18x). (3) The gain comes entirely from planets: +62/-7, p=4e-12. Injections are a wash: +32/-26, p=0.51, recall 0.293 -> 0.308. H1's predicted injection gain toward 0.55 is not supported. The 33 losses are 26 injections and 7 planets, spread across P = 0.8-10.9 d, with no loss above 10.9 d. Injection recall falls with period: P 3-7 d 28 -> 22, 7-10 d 10 -> 5, 10-13.5 d 7 -> 4, so long-period injection recall roughly halves (17 -> 9). The event-count/dominance penalty therefore does cost real long-period signals, as D2 feared. TIC 111778581 (P=11.42 d, 41150 ppm) was missed by both baseline and H1, so it is an unfixed miss, not a regression. Planets with P>=7 d improved slightly (4 -> 7). Also, D2's 'budget of 2 spent' fits the H1 full run already being in flight (file written 02:21). Actions: promote, but claim only a planet-recall gain. Before the blind evaluation, test a softer penalty (per-event consistency rather than a hard count of 3) and track recall for P>=7 d injections.

record.title: Time-windowed Tukey biweight slider is the best general detrender for transit discovery
record.body: Hippke+2019 benchmarked common detrenders on hundreds of Kepler/K2/TESS small planets; a time-windowed biweight slider recovered 99%/94% of the shallowest Kepler/K2 planets. For us: wotan biweight (window ~3x longest duration) is a cheap, robust default for QLP FFI; gap-edge masking is our own addition, not tested in this abstract.

record.title: Kepler TPS accepts signals on SNR plus periodicity plus separate false-positive veto tests, not on SNR alone
record.body: Tenenbaum+2013 (Q1-Q12 TPS): detections required periodicity, adequate SNR and three tests that reject false positives. For us: replace the hard <3-transit penalty (H1) with an explicit consistency veto (e.g. per-transit SNR agreement / chi-square of individual events) so 2-transit signals survive on their own merits. Abstract does not detail the tests; specifics (MES/SES, chi-square) need the full paper.

record.title: Long-period (P>25 d) and single/few-transit events are a sizeable share of TESS FFI yield
record.body: TIaRA (2024) injection-recovery on real TESS Y1+Y3 SPOC FFI light curves predicts ~2271 detectable planets, ~215 from single transits plus more from duotransits. For us: penalising <3 transits throws away a real population; our injection recall drop at long period (N1) is consistent with this, so H1 penalty should be softened, not tuned harder.

record.title: Surveys deliberately search for TESS signals with one transit per sector (duotransits) at P>20 d
record.body: Gill-style duotransit search of TESS S. Ecliptic Cycles 1+3 found 85 candidates (depths 0.1-1.8%) from one transit per year. For us: low-event signals are routinely kept as candidates when depth is significant; supports scoring 1-2 event signals by depth SNR plus shape checks rather than a hard event-count penalty.

record.title: [agent-generated] Replace H1 hard <3-event penalty with depth-SNR + per-event consistency veto to recover long-period injections
record.body: Champion dev-7227ffda (R4): injection recall 0.308; recall_by_depth injected 0-1000 ppm 5/126, 1000-3000 40/142. N1: H1 event-count penalty halves P>=7 d injection recall vs baseline (injected gained 32/lost 26, p=0.51, i.e. no injected gain at all). Controls do not need the penalty to stay quiet if 1-2 event signals must pass a per-transit consistency check (E10) - single-event systematics fail it, real duotransits (E11,E12) pass. Change: score = depth SNR (red-noise-scaled) for all signals; drop event-count multiplier; veto/downweight when per-event depth chi2 is inconsistent or odd/even differ >3 sigma. Errors note: H2/H3 run JSONs (R5,R6) store only error counts; harness.py:73 builds 'Type: msg' but results are not persisted, so causes are unrecoverable from runs/. A smoke test of h2/h3 on 3 multi-gap dev stars (no NaNs in any of 18 dev curves checked) raised nothing, so errors are star-specific (likely degenerate arrays after masking/clipping, e.g. empty BLS input or zero-MAD windows). Pipeline must wrap per-stage steps and fall back rather than raise.

data.mechanism: H1 multiplies score by an event-count penalty, so true 1-2 transit signals at P>=7 d fall under the 5% FA threshold (16.66); replacing it with depth-SNR plus a per-event consistency veto keeps those while still rejecting single-event systematics that drive control false alarms
data.expected_score_gain: +0.03 to +0.05 (injection recall +0.06-0.10 from long-period recovery, planet recall flat)
data.test: Quick run (10 min) of pipelines/h4_consistency.py vs H1 quick dev-55fcddcf on matched targets: pass if injected P>=7 d recall >= baseline dev-8f6a421c, control false alarms at threshold <=7/145 and errors == 0; then full run (25 min) for promotion vs dev-7227ffda

record.title: [agent-generated] H3's gain is real but hidden by 14 per-star exceptions: error-proof H3 detrend/mask and its lower control false-alarm threshold lifts score without touching the penalty
record.body: Competing with the penalty hypothesis: misses are driven by the control threshold, not by event counts. H3 quick dev-69591abb (R5) scores 0.4203 vs H1 quick 0.414 with threshold 12.0 vs 16.7 for the champion (R4): biweight detrend + gap-edge masking (E9) removes the variability/gap-edge events that make controls score high, so a lower threshold admits more shallow signals (injected 1000-3000 ppm 15/45=33% vs champion 40/142=28%; planet 1000-3000 10/18 vs 8/36). But 14/225 stars errored (signals=[] so they count as misses, and promotion is blocked by lab.py:94). H2 dev-7af97ddd (R6) is a broken run: 18 errors and 0 recovered on all 225 targets even for >10000 ppm planets, so its score of 0 says nothing about detrending; it should be rerun once fixed, not read as a negative result. Error cause: harness.py:73 records 'Type: msg' per star but the messages are not written to runs/*.json, so they cannot be read back. A smoke test on 3 multi-gap dev stars ran clean and none of 18 dev curves had NaNs, so the failures come from edge cases: windows/segments left empty or with zero MAD after edge masking and clipping (BLS on empty or too-short arrays, or argmax on all-NaN power). Fix: guard every stage (min points, finite power), fall back to unmasked H1 path, and persist error strings in outcomes.

data.mechanism: Robust detrend + gap-edge masking lowers control scores (threshold 16.7 -> ~12), raising recall of shallow transits; the 14 errored stars are scored as misses and block promotion, so guarding them recovers both score and promotability
data.expected_score_gain: +0.02 to +0.04 over the champion (H3 quick already +0.006 over H1 quick with 6% of stars zeroed by errors)
data.test: Patch h3_combined.py with stage guards + fallback; smoke-test on the dev stars (<20) then quick run (10 min) vs dev-69591abb on matched targets: pass if errors == 0, threshold <=13 and score >= 0.43; also persist per-star error strings in harness outcomes

record.title: Round 2 plan: test H4 (soft event penalty) and H5 (crash-proof H3) in parallel
record.body: Options considered: H4 replace H1's hard <3-transit penalty with depth SNR + per-event consistency (+0.03-0.05, 35 min); H5 guard H3 (biweight+gap mask+wide grid on H1 scoring) against the 14 star errors with a fallback (+0.02-0.04, 15 min quick); rerun H2 after fix (broken run R6, low value alone since H3 subsumes it); TLS (E2,E3; runtime risk, deferred); red-noise SNR (E6,E7; deferred); CETRA (E4; rewrite, deferred); harness change to save per-star error messages (not a pipeline hypothesis; flagged for a person). Chosen: H4 and H5 (budget limited to two engineers by time). Why: they attack the two measured losses: N1 long-period injection loss (H4, supported by E10-E12) and H3's quick gain hidden by crashes (H5, E9). Both are cheap. H5 has the best learning per minute because H3 already beat the H1 quick with 14 errors. H2 rerun is dropped because H3 contains it. Each engineer: smoke test, quick run, full run only if quick beats the H1 quick dev-55fcddcf (0.414) with 0 errors. Full runs are serialised by the lab lock.

record.title: Restricting the trial-duration grid to the range of known planets (with stellar density priors) keeps TLS fast, and SDE thresholds can be calibrated by injection-recovery on quiet stars
record.body: Hippke & Heller introduce TLS, which searches the unbinned phase-folded light curve with a limb-darkened transit shape and limits trial durations to the range that covers all known planets, using stellar density priors where available. They calibrate SDE thresholds with Earth-size injection-recovery in 110 ppm white noise (a quiet Kp=12 Kepler star). For us: tie the duration grid to the period through stellar density so short-period transits are covered, and set the SDE cut using injections into our own quiet-star noise.

record.title: A time-windowed biweight slider is the best general-purpose detrender for keeping shallow transits
record.body: Wotan benchmarks the common detrending methods on hundreds of difficult Kepler, K2 and TESS small-planet systems, testing each method's full parameter range. The best method was a time-windowed slider with an iterative Tukey biweight location estimator, which recovered 99% of the shallowest Kepler planets and 94% of the shallowest K2 planets. For us: use a biweight sliding window and sweep its length when tuning; the abstract does not give the window-to-duration rule, so we need to measure that ourselves.

record.title: Automated vetting against noise and systematics can keep high completeness while reaching high reliability, measured with injected transits and simulated false alarms
record.body: The Kepler DR25 Robovetter uses metric-based vetoes on TCEs, calibrated with simulated transits, simulated systematic noise and simulated false positives. For P<100 d it kept more than 85% of injected transits and reached more than 98% reliability against instrumental and stellar noise, but completeness and reliability both fell for low-SNR long-period signals. For us: add vetoes after the search rather than raising the SDE threshold, and measure their effect on recall and false alarms with injections plus inverted or scrambled light curves.

record.title: [agent-generated] H6: red-noise-aware SNR in h1_robust_snr lowers the control threshold
record.body: Evidence: misses dev-7227ffda; the 8 deepest misses are missed by champion dev-7227ffda, H5 dev-999d74ff and baseline dev-8f6a421c alike. Quick script on 6 of them (h1 search): ALL found at the true period (<0.3% error, matching tolerance 1%), detrended dip ~= raw dip (no detrending loss), but top scores 7.3/8.0/11.6/16.5/15.6/7.6 vs threshold 16.66. These are faint stars (per-point MAD 11k-42k ppm). TIC 115018003 (16.5) and 442381495 (15.6) sit just under threshold. Miss mechanism is score vs threshold, not alias/grid/detrending. Control top scores are NOT stored in run JSON, so the threshold-setting controls could not be identified directly (open gap). Claim: robust_snr_score uses white-noise sigma (per-point MAD * sqrt(n_in)); quiet bright controls with correlated systematics (scattered light, momentum dumps) get inflated SNR and set the 16.66 threshold, while the threshold moved to 17.99 when only detrending changed (H5), consistent with systematics-driven control tails.

data.mechanism: In robust_snr_score replace sigma*sqrt(n_in) with a red-noise term: sigma_dur = robust std (MAD) of the detrended out-of-transit flux binned to the trial duration, total_snr = depth/sigma_dur*sqrt(n_events). Correlated-noise controls are deflated more than white-noise faint planets, so the 5% threshold falls relative to planet scores.
data.expected_score_gain: +0.02 to +0.05 (threshold drop recovers near-threshold deep planets such as TIC 115018003/442381495 and 3000-10000 ppm injections)
data.test: FULL dev run vs champion dev-7227ffda: promote only if paired net gain >0 with sign-test p<0.05 and score > 0.3489; also check TIC 115018003 and 442381495 recovered, and that the threshold/median-control-score ratio fell. Do not use a quick run (D4).

record.title: [agent-generated] H7: finer duration grid and best-duration scoring in h1_robust_snr raise deep-planet scores
record.body: Evidence: misses dev-7227ffda; the 8 deepest misses are missed by champion dev-7227ffda, H5 dev-999d74ff and baseline dev-8f6a421c alike. Quick script on 6 of them (h1 search): ALL found at the true period (<0.3% error, matching tolerance 1%), detrended dip ~= raw dip (no detrending loss), but top scores 7.3/8.0/11.6/16.5/15.6/7.6 vs threshold 16.66. These are faint stars (per-point MAD 11k-42k ppm). TIC 115018003 (16.5) and 442381495 (15.6) sit just under threshold. Miss mechanism is score vs threshold, not alias/grid/detrending. Control top scores are NOT stored in run JSON, so the threshold-setting controls could not be identified directly (open gap). Competing claim: the lever is on the planet side, not the control side. BLS picks a duration from the coarse [0.04,0.08,0.16] grid (TIC 115018003 true 0.058 d fit at 0.04; 31061885 0.070 at 0.04; 51217656 0.094 at 0.08), so the in-transit box under-collects signal and the SNR used for scoring is lower than the matched one.

data.mechanism: Set DURATIONS_DAYS = [0.03,0.045,0.06,0.08,0.11,0.16] and, after BLS picks period/t0, compute robust_snr_score at each grid duration and keep the maximum (report that duration). Detection and the threshold rule are unchanged; matched-duration SNR lifts planets that are just under threshold, but controls gain little because their peaks are not box-shaped.
data.expected_score_gain: +0.01 to +0.03 (mainly near-threshold deep planets; risk: maximising over durations also inflates control tails, which raises the threshold)
data.cost_minutes: ~5 code + 30 full run (about 2x BLS durations, +~30% s/star)
data.test: FULL dev run vs champion dev-7227ffda: promote only if paired net gain >0 with sign-test p<0.05 and score > 0.3489; report the threshold change (if it rises above ~17.5, the control-side H6 explanation is favoured). Do not use a quick run (D4).

record.title: Round 3 plan: test H6 (correlated-noise SNR) and H7 (finer duration grid) as full runs
record.body: Options considered: H6 score with a noise estimate from flux binned to the transit duration, which deflates controls with systematics (+0.02-0.05, ~35 min; E13, E7). H7 finer duration grid 0.03-0.16 d, scoring at the best duration (+0.01-0.03, ~35 min, ~30% slower per star; E13). H4 full run of the soft event-count penalty (quick result in noise per D4; untested on full). Biweight window-length sweep (E14; H5 lost on full, so detrending is deprioritised). Post-search vetoes (E15; larger build). Harness change to persist control scores and per-star errors (not a pipeline change; flagged for a person). Chosen: H6 and H7. Why: the analyst showed that the 8 deepest misses are found at the right period but score below 16.66, so the gain lies in the score/threshold balance, and these two attack it from the control side and the planet side. Each is a cheap single change to H1. About 1h40m remains, enough for two serialised full runs and no third. Per D4, no quick gate: smoke test on <10 dev stars with 0 errors, then one full run each. H4 stays open for a later round.

record.title: H6 full dev run dev-79de03f3: duration-binned (correlated) noise SNR scores 0.3419 vs champion 0.3489; net -2 (gained 11, lost 13, p=0.84)
record.body: pipelines/h6_binned_noise.py = h1_robust_snr with the SNR noise term changed to the MAD of out-of-transit detrended flux binned to the trial duration (sigma_dur); total_snr = depth/sigma_dur*sqrt(n_events), with per-event SNR = event depth/sigma_dur. Nothing else changed. Smoke test: 8 dev stars (incl. TIC 115018003, 442381495), 0 errors. Full dev run dev-79de03f3 (recorded by hand: the CLI hit the KeyError 'outcomes' in compare_to_champion after saving the run). Score 0.3419 (champion dev-7227ffda 0.3489, delta -0.0070). Planet recall 0.368 (vs 0.3896), injection recall 0.3158 (vs 0.3083). Threshold 15.52 (vs 16.66), 20/399 control FAs, 0 errors, median 10.7 s/star (vs 13.7; same code path, so this difference is noise in machine load). Paired vs dev-7227ffda: gained 11, lost 13, net -2, sign-test p=0.84. By depth: planet 3000-10000 ppm 28/64 (vs 35/64), planet 1000-3000 10/36 (vs 8/36), injected 3000-10000 82/131 (vs 78/131), injected 1000-3000 38/142 (vs 40/142). TIC 115018003 and 442381495 are still missed (smoke scores 15.2 and 15.1, vs 16.5 and 15.6 under H1). The threshold fell by about 7%, but scores of real planets fell by a similar or larger amount, so the score/threshold balance did not improve. The threshold/median-control-score ratio cannot be computed because control scores are not stored in the run JSON. Not promoted.

record.title: Full dev run of pipelines/h7_fine_duration.py (H7): 0.329, worse than champion (net -13, p=0.001)
record.body: Run dev-c52c370a, full dev, 0 errors. The CLI ran the experiment but crashed in _record_dev_result (harness passes the in-memory run, which has no 'outcomes', to lab.compare_to_champion: KeyError 'outcomes'). The run JSON was saved, so this entry was recorded by hand, with the paired comparison computed by lab.paired_comparison(load_run('dev-c52c370a'), load_run('dev-7227ffda')). Change vs H1: DURATIONS_DAYS [0.03,0.045,0.06,0.08,0.11,0.16]; the robust SNR is evaluated at every grid duration at the BLS period/t0 and the max is kept (that duration is reported); frequency_factor=0.04/0.03 keeps H1's 27,825-period grid (without it, the smoke test was +54% slower). Score 0.3290 vs 0.3489 (delta -0.0199); planet recall 0.3723 vs 0.3896; injection recall 0.2857 vs 0.3083. Threshold rose to 18.08 from 16.66 (20/399 control FAs both). Median s/star 13.16 vs 13.73 (no measurable slowdown; the smoke test showed about x1.17 pipeline time). Paired: gained 1, lost 14, net -13, sign-test p=0.001. TIC 115018003 and 442381495 still missed (smoke scores 16.93 and 16.41 are below the new 18.08 threshold). Reading: maximising the score over durations inflates the control tail more than it lifts planets. The threshold rose above the ~17.5 marker in H7's test, which favours the control-side (H6) explanation.

record.title: Round 3: no promotion; changes to the score statistic move control and planet scores together
record.body: What changed: nothing; the champion stays H1 dev-7227ffda (0.3489). H6 binned-noise SNR full dev-79de03f3: 0.3419, threshold 16.66->15.52, gained 11/lost 13, p=0.84 (R11). H7 fine duration grid full dev-c52c370a: 0.3290, threshold 18.08, gained 1/lost 14, p=0.001 (R12). Learned: lowering the threshold (H6) and raising planet scores (H7) both failed for the same reason. Each change moved the control stars' top scores in proportion with the faint planets'. The near-threshold planets TIC 115018003/442381495 stayed below threshold in both. This reopens the assumption behind H6/H7 (and P3) that a separable control population with systematics sets the threshold. With one-dimensional SNR scoring, controls and faint planets look alike, so further rescaling of SNR is unlikely to pay. H7's reading that its result favours H6 is contradicted by R11. Next: attack separation, not scale. Use shape and consistency vetoes applied after the search (E15; per-transit depth consistency, odd/even, transit shape vs box) on the champion's top signals. Run H4 (soft event penalty) on the full split, since it was never tested there. Fix the harness first: per-control top-signal scores and per-star errors are needed to see what sets the threshold, and the experiment CLI crashes in compare_to_champion/_record_dev_result (KeyError 'outcomes') on every full run. Two rounds in a row failed to improve; the protocol would now call for the evaluator, but per instruction it is not dispatched.

record.title: Lab summary after rounds 1-3
record.body: Measured improvement: the champion H1 (pipelines/h1_robust_snr.py, dev-7227ffda) scores 0.3489 on the full dev split vs 0.2224 for the baseline dev-8f6a421c (+0.127, +57% relative), all from round 1. Rounds 2-3 tested H4 (quick only, 0.409 vs 0.414 gate), H5 (full 0.3103), H6 (full 0.3419) and H7 (full 0.3290); none beat the champion, so there were no promotions and the skeptic was not needed. Methodological lesson (D4): quick runs (145 controls) set too noisy a threshold to rank pipelines; use full runs. Scientific lesson (D5): the deepest misses are found at the right period but score below threshold on faint stars, and rescaling SNR moves control and planet scores together. Blind evaluation: not run, since the evaluator was not dispatched per instruction, so generalisation beyond dev is unmeasured. Candidates: none, since the vetter was not dispatched. Next experiment: fix the harness to persist control top-signal scores and per-star errors, and fix the KeyError 'outcomes' crash. Then run a full dev run of H1 plus post-search shape/consistency vetoes (E15: per-transit depth agreement, odd/even, box-vs-trapezoid shape) to separate faint planets from control false alarms, and a full run of H4 as the second arm.

record.title: Holdout score for pipelines/h1_robust_snr.py
Blind holdout: champion H1 recovers 5 of 37 post-cutoff TOIs at a 5% false-alarm rate (score 0.209 vs 0.349 on dev)
record.body: Holdout run holdout-c88b13b5. Planet recall 0.135 (dev 0.390), injection recall 0.283 (dev 0.308). The 5% false-alarm threshold set by the 399 holdout control stars is 23.5 vs 16.7 on dev, and the 1% threshold is 94.6, so a few holdout controls carry extreme systematics that raise the bar. Injection recall nearly holds, so detection generalises; the threshold does not. Recovered: TOI 7867.01, 7877.01, 7880.01, 7889.01, 7897.01, all deep (8,000-126,000 ppm). This supports the round-3 finding (D5) that one global score threshold is the bottleneck, and argues for a per-star noise model or a separate vetting stage before thresholding. Baseline holdout pending for the blind comparison.

record.title: Holdout score for pipelines/baseline.py
Blind holdout reverses the dev result: baseline 0.263 vs champion H1 0.209; H1's gain was a dev-set artifact
record.body: Baseline holdout-5328e37d: score 0.263, planet recall 0.189 (7/37), injection recall 0.336, 5% threshold 16.9 (dev 17.1). H1 holdout-c88b13b5: score 0.209, planet 0.135 (5/37), injection 0.283, threshold 23.5 (dev 16.7). Paired on identical holdout targets, H1 vs baseline: planets +1/-3 (p=0.63), injected transits +14/-35 (p=0.004). Mechanism: the baseline's SDE is normalised by each star's own periodogram, so its false-alarm threshold is stable across control samples; H1's per-signal robust SNR has a heavy tail on rare systematics that occur among holdout controls but not dev controls, so its threshold jumped and pushed real transits under it. The dev comparisons (R4, net +61) were valid on dev but did not generalise. Next experiment: normalise H1's per-signal SNR by the star's own periodogram distribution (an SDE-style calibration), and grow the dev control set so rare systematics appear before promotion; score once more on a fresh holdout.

record.title: Discovery search: 0 signals above threshold, 0 pass automated vetting
Discovery: no new candidates among 300 unlabelled stars at the strict (1% false-alarm) threshold
record.body: Champion H1 searched 300 QLP stars from sectors 96-98 with no TOI or CTOI. No signal reached the strict threshold of 66.0 (the 99th percentile of dev control top scores), so nothing went to vetting. Given N4 (H1's score has a heavy tail on rare systematics), this threshold is conservative. Next: rerun discovery with the recalibrated pipeline proposed in N4 over all 1,499 stars, and review the top-ranked signals with the vetting checks rather than a single cut.
